requirements.requirement: curl is held/locked at its current installed version on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline curl-7.76.1-40.el9 captured, python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock installed, and a versionlock entry for curl-0:7.76.1-40.el9.* added and confirmed listed.

requirements.requirement: A system update leaves curl at its held version while other packages update normally
requirements.summary: A full 'dnf update -y' was run; many packages (kernel, NetworkManager, systemd, coreutils, etc.) were upgraded/installed, while curl remained curl-7.76.1-40.el9.x86_64 both before and after, and the versionlock.list file on disk still contained the curl lock entry.

requirements.requirement: Hold persists (durable configuration, not just in-memory)
requirements.summary: versionlock.list on disk (/etc/dnf/plugins/versionlock.list) contained the curl entry after the update and again after the subsequent reboot, indicating the lock is a persistent config file.

requirements.requirement: (Independent) provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with pre/post boot identity, restart ack, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 55595e92... and healthy curl/versionlock state captured, systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged via stream closure, node polled through timeouts until it returned with a new boot_id bb3a7c3b..., and post-restart state re-verified curl unchanged and versionlock still active. Cross-checked by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot showing bb3a7c3b-78c8-48f3-837c-62277a2fd01b, matching the executor's captured post-restart boot_id, and by the platform diff showing the expected kernel package version bump.

overall_summary: The executor successfully installed and configured a dnf versionlock hold on curl, ran a full system update that upgraded numerous other packages while leaving curl untouched, and confirmed the versionlock configuration persisted on disk. It additionally completed the independent node-restart evidence protocol on node1 with a directly observed boot-identity change and recovered curl/versionlock state post-reboot, cross-confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. All observed state-changing commands were purposeful and bounded, with negligible residue.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured; no additional disruption scenarios (e.g., service crash, longer outage) were tested, though none were required by the task.

The dnf versionlock 'status' subcommand was unsupported in this dnf version, so the executor fell back to an rpm package-presence check as a proxy for plugin activity; a minor substitution that doesn't affect the core evidence of the hold persisting.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map clearly to task requirements: installing the versionlock plugin and adding the curl lock (prerequisite for the hold), running a full 'dnf update -y' (bounded evidence to demonstrate the hold survives an update), and issuing systemctl reboot (required by the independent restart-evidence protocol). No failed services, no exposed ports beyond pre-existing sshd/chronyd, and dnf package-health checks report clean both before and after. The only minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, an artifact automatically produced by the nohup-wrapped reboot command itself, a low-risk expected byproduct of the mandated restart step rather than an unnecessary mutation.
